text:
Marathon Petroleum stock fell slightly today despite oil prices surging above $100 a barrel—the first time since May—driven by escalating Iran war tensions. The company is running refineries at 98% capacity with healthy product inventories, so the small decline appears to be profit-taking after the stock jumped nearly 10% over two weeks riding the oil rally, rather than a sign of weakness in the underlying business.

The broader context is that refining margins are being supported by elevated crude prices and strong demand signals (storage levels are moderate, not bloated), but the geopolitical premium in oil markets may be reaching a point where investors are pausing before the midterm elections, which some expect could shift energy policy.
